paragraphs: Posted by Lily. Every Thursday, one Explorer gives a short talk in the school library. This week, Mia talked about worms in the school garden. She wrote her own notes first, and I wrote her talk for the blog afterwards. Mia loves small animals, and the school garden is her favorite place. Teacher Kim read the talk, and here it is.

"Hey, everybody, do you know a small animal that works under your feet?" "It is a worm, and it has no legs, no eyes, and no ears." "Many people think that worms are not important, but they have three big jobs." "First, worms make the soil better." "They eat dead leaves, and they leave very good food for plants." "Here is an example." "The Explorers have two garden boxes." "We put worms in only one box." "After four weeks, the plants in the box with worms were taller."

"Second, worms make small holes in the soil." "Air and water go down through the holes to the roots of plants." "Here is another example." "One day, it rained hard, and we looked at both boxes." "The water level in the box with no worms stayed high on the top." "In the box with worms, the water went down in a few minutes."

"Third, worms are food for other animals." "Birds, frogs, and some fish eat them." "One morning, we sat near the garden and watched." "A small bird came, pulled a worm out of the grass, and flew away." "Then a second bird came and did the same, and both birds looked very happy." "Without worms, these birds may not find enough food."

"Now, what can we do?" "Please do not worry when you see a worm on the ground." "It is not dangerous, and it is not dirty." "Do not step on it, and do not put it in the sun, because the sun is hot for it." "Teacher Kim gave us a document with three garden rules." "Rule one says that we keep a box of dry leaves in the garden." "Rule two says that we put old fruit in the garden box." "Rule three says that we never use strong soap near the soil."
"Worms are small, but they work all day and all night." "Thank you for listening, and please look after our garden workers."

sentences.text: Posted by Lily.
Every Thursday, one Explorer gives a short talk in the school library.
This week, Mia talked about worms in the school garden.
She wrote her own notes first, and I wrote her talk for the blog afterwards.
Mia loves small animals, and the school garden is her favorite place.
Teacher Kim read the talk, and here it is.
"Hey, everybody, do you know a small animal that works under your feet?"
"It is a worm, and it has no legs, no eyes, and no ears."
"Many people think that worms are not important, but they have three big jobs."
"First, worms make the soil better."
"They eat dead leaves, and they leave very good food for plants."
"Here is an example."
"The Explorers have two garden boxes."
"We put worms in only one box."
"After four weeks, the plants in the box with worms were taller."
"Second, worms make small holes in the soil."
"Air and water go down through the holes to the roots of plants."
"Here is another example."
"One day, it rained hard, and we looked at both boxes."
"The water level in the box with no worms stayed high on the top."
"In the box with worms, the water went down in a few minutes."
"Third, worms are food for other animals."
"Birds, frogs, and some fish eat them."
"One morning, we sat near the garden and watched."
"A small bird came, pulled a worm out of the grass, and flew away."
"Then a second bird came and did the same, and both birds looked very happy."
"Without worms, these birds may not find enough food."
"Now, what can we do?"
"Please do not worry when you see a worm on the ground."
"It is not dangerous, and it is not dirty."
"Do not step on it, and do not put it in the sun, because the sun is hot for it."
"Teacher Kim gave us a document with three garden rules."
"Rule one says that we keep a box of dry leaves in the garden."
"Rule two says that we put old fruit in the garden box."
"Rule three says that we never use strong soap near the soil."
"Worms are small, but they work all day and all night."
"Thank you for listening, and please look after our garden workers."
